//: One SRAM per engine, in a row along the bottom, 400 um apart: 8 stripe pitches, so each one lines up with the stripes the same way. Mirrored (MX) so the signal pins, all on one edge, face up into the logic instead of the die edge.

The row sits 11.34 um from the die edge: the rows under it are inside the 10 um macro halo, so no cells go below an SRAM. At 37.8 um the cells placed under SRAM 1 had to reach the logic over it, and the router left 65 shorts there with the SRAM power columns.
SRAM: the power stripes are placed so some land on the SRAM power columns; Pemu.BridgeSramPower joins them (see scripts/bridge_sram_power.py).
VGND stripe 5.62 um after VPWR, the SRAM VDD-to-VSS column spacing
Two passes left four nets over the antenna ratio, so I allow five.
Set explicitly: left unset, this LibreLane version passes '-threads None' and OpenROAD falls back to one thread.

If you get stuck with this config, please open an issue or get in touch via the discord.
Here are some of the variables you may want to change:
PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT - You can increase this if Global Placement fails with error GPL-0302.
Users have reported that values up to 80 worked well for them.
CLOCK_PERIOD - Increase this in case you are getting setup time violations.
The value is in nanoseconds, so 20ns == 50MHz.
The chip runs at 50 MHz. Setup is signed off at that clock at the typical and fast
corners; at the slow one (1.08 V, 125 C) the longest path is about 23 ns, so there it is
good for about 43 MHz (docs/info.md). Hold is checked at every corner. The resizer
still works against the slow corner: before routing it only has wire estimates, and the
slow corner came out up to 6 ns worse once routed, so it aims 5 ns tighter there and
repairs again with the real wires after global routing.
After global routing the estimate was still about 3 ns optimistic (the resizer saw no
path under 1 ns of slack, the routed slow corner was at -2.06 ns), so the second repair
aims 2 ns tighter.
Without a slew limit the slow corner had x1 gates driving long wires with 3 to 5 ns of delay
each. 1.5 ns makes the design repair buffer or upsize those nets.
Map for area and leave timing to the resizer after placement. With LibreLane 3.1.0.dev4 the
default DELAY 4 strategy added about 11,000 buffers in synthesis (+34% area) and routing
no longer finished in 6 hours.
Hold slack margin - Increase them in case you are getting hold violations.
Five paths into an SRAM address missed hold by up to 0.07 ns at the fast corner once the
post-route repair was on, so the post-global-route margin went from 0.05 to 0.15,
then to 0.25 after two paths still missed by up to 0.018 ns. The
placement margin stays at 0.1: hold is repaired again after global routing, where the
real violators are known.
RUN_LINTER, LINTER_INCLUDE_PDK_MODELS - Disabling the linter is not recommended!
If you need a custom clock configuration, read the following documentation first:
https://tinytapeout.com/faq/#how-can-i-map-an-additional-external-clock-to-one-of-the-gpios
Configuration docs: https://librelane.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/configuration.html
